text:
kevin: Customer on prod started seeing intermittent 504s around our /v1/generate endpoint, then client retries kick in and we get a spike of downstream errors. They say it started after upgrading to our Go SDK v1.4.0. Any quick ideas?

jia: can you paste a minimal repro and the Go runtime version + net/http stats? also which transport config they use (custom http.Client or default)?

kevin: repro is simple, they create a fresh http.Client per request and use a context with a 2s timeout. snippet below — this is from their support case: 

```
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 2*time.Second)
defer cancel()

req, _ := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, "POST", url, strings.NewReader(body))
client := &http.Client{Timeout: 3 * time.Second}
resp, err := client.Do(req)
if err != nil {
  return err
}
// handle resp but sometimes code returns early and doesn't drain body
return nil
```

kevin: they also show logs where we timed out, then retry layer issues a second request immediately. connections on the host spike then start getting "unexpected EOF" and 504s.

amar: this is a classic conn reuse / drain issue + inefficient client usage. creating a new http.Client per request means the Transport can't reuse connections well and you risk exhausting sockets. also if you cancel ctx before draining + closing resp.Body the underlying connection may not be re-used which increases dial churn.

jia: +1. ask them to try 3 things: 1) reuse a single http.Client (one global) with tuned Transport, 2) always read or drain and close resp.Body (or call io.Copy(io.Discard, resp.Body) then Close), 3) prefer using request context for per-request cancel but avoid overlapping that with client Timeout unless intended.

kevin: any recommended Transport settings to share with the customer?

amar: here's a conservative Transport config we recommend for high-throughput clients: 

```
tr := &http.Transport{
  Proxy: http.ProxyFromEnvironment,
  DialContext: (&net.Dialer{Timeout: 30 * time.Second, KeepAlive: 30 * time.Second}).DialContext,
  ForceAttemptHTTP2: true,
  MaxIdleConns: 100,
  MaxIdleConnsPerHost: 100,
  IdleConnTimeout: 90 * time.Second,
  TLSHandshakeTimeout: 10 * time.Second,
  ExpectContinueTimeout: 1 * time.Second,
}
client := &http.Client{Transport: tr}
```

amar: also explain that client.Timeout cancels the whole request including body reads — combining that with a short request context can cause early cancellation. prefer context.WithTimeout on req and a longer client.Timeout or zero (no global timeout) on shared client.

jia: another thing: when our SDK retry layer retries on context deadline, ensure the original request's body isn't a non-rewindable stream. if body is io.ReadCloser that can't be re-read, retries will fail or you have to buffer it. many customers hit this when using streaming payloads.

kevin: noted. i'll send these suggestions to the customer and ask them to try a quick patch: reuse client + drain/close body + bump timeouts. i'll also ask for net/http trace + `GODEBUG=http2debug=1` logs if it persists.

kevin: thanks all, will follow up once they test. :thumbsup:
